w: A can't-miss Beavercreek hidden gem: the Dayton Daily News profiled this 'inconspicuous little pink building' as cranking out some of the best authentic Thai food in Dayton, singling out the tamarind-coated pad thai and the crunchy fried bananas. Family-run and generous with portions; Dayton Local (Gem City) lists it among the area's top Thai. Google/RestaurantGuru strong across 230+ reviews.

A family-owned Riverside room (near Wright-Patterson) serving authentic Vietnamese and Chinese since the 1980s — about 15 pho broths including vegetarian, plus banh mi and vermicelli. Named in Dayton937's 'Quest for the Best Pho' as one of the region's genuine pho stops ($10–12 for pho, roll and tea); regulars call it the best Vietnamese in Dayton, with 400+ reviews behind it.

address: 2733 Fairfield Commons Unit A, Beavercreek, OH 45431
w: A distinctive Viet-Cajun mashup at Fairfield Commons (the former Flyby BBQ space): build-your-own Cajun seafood boils — crawfish, crab, shrimp, mussels with corn and potatoes — alongside a full Vietnamese menu of pho, grilled-pork vermicelli and pork-chop rice. Both the Dayton Daily News and Dayton937 covered the opening; one Vietnamese reviewer called its pho the best in Dayton.

dish: boba tea, Vietnamese coffee, Korean corn dogs
w: A Taiwanese bubble-tea shop and Vietnamese deli — boba, bubble waffles, mochi donuts, Korean corn dogs and Vietnamese-style coffees and smoothies. The Dayton Daily News tracked the local mini-chain to its third location at The Greene in Beavercreek; popularity across its Riverside and Miamisburg shops carried it to the region's premier retail center.

Beavercreek's viral conveyor-belt sushi arrival (former Jason's Deli space): nigiri, sashimi and specialty rolls rotate past on a belt, with iPad ordering at each table. The Dayton Daily News covered its July soft opening and WDTN tracked the Cincinnati-born concept to Beavercreek; a CityBeat review praised the freshness and 'all around excellent' service. Google 4.5 out of the gate.

dish: fish-noodle soup (五谷鱼粉), mala beef noodle
w: A specialist Chinese noodle house in Kettering built around southern-Chinese fish-noodle soup — bouncy rice noodles, fish, fried yellow peas on the side and a build-your-own spice level via pepper oils. Owners Yaqin Jing and Zeng Siong ran four restaurants in southern China before opening here; Dayton937 gave it a dedicated feature. Google 4.7 / RestaurantGuru 4.6 across 130+ reviews — a genuine hidden gem, not a generic buffet.

An upscale, metropolitan sushi-and-Asian room in Kettering with a bar and patio. The Dayton Daily News 'First Look' said it impresses and singled out impeccably fresh fish on rolls like the 5th Ave.; Dayton937's Jon Hung called it 'a gem you have to try.' Google 4.5 across 280–380 reviews — the area's higher-end sushi standout.

Chef Dane Shipp's second concept (after Culture in the Oregon District), inside The Silos food hall downtown: Asian-inspired hot and cold noodles, bao and dumplings rooted in the Lao home-cooking Shipp learned from former roommates — e.g. a chicken ramen finished with collards. WDTN's Living Dayton featured its signature menu and the Dayton Daily News covered it as The Silos' debut vendor; Cincinnati/Dayton creator CutieTheFoodie (~51.7K TikTok) filmed the ramen, bao and street corn on site.
